Hi Aditya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our tech leadership wants clarity on two things before we move the deal to legal: 1) how are uptime credits calculated for sub-month incidents (we bill on a calendar month) and 2) whether premium escalation coverage (24x7 on-call with named engineers) is billed as a recurring flat fee or on a usage basis during incidents.

We have a predictable bursty pattern (monthly ETL jobs) and procurement is pushing for a proration model that aligns credits/charges to the calendar billing period. Any chance you can share how Redwood structures this? Also please include any attachments that show the credit formula and on-call roster.

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary up front: we support calendar-month billing and per-month uptime credits (not per-incident billing), and premium escalation (named on-call coverage) is offered as a monthly add-on that can be prorated mid-cycle with a defined rule set. I attached a short ratesheet and an escalation chart for clarity.

Key points (short):
- Uptime credits: calculated monthly as a percentage of the monthly invoice. If monthly uptime falls below an SLA threshold, the credit is X% of that invoice (examples on pg.2 of SLA_Ratesheet_v2.pdf). We compute uptime across the region(s) you pin in the contract.
- Sub-month incidents: credits are applied to the month where the incident occurred; we do not split credits across adjacent months. That aligns with calendar billing and keeps invoicing predictable.
- Proration for upgrades: if you add premium escalation mid-billing-cycle we prorate the add-on for the remaining calendar days.
- On-call model: standard (business hours) vs premium (24x7 named rotation). Premium is a recurring monthly commitment but includes a per-incident override rate for extraordinary incident work beyond agreed hours.

As a negotiation option, we can offer a blended SLA tier (99.95% core + 99.99% critical endpoints) with a 12-month commitment in exchange for a 10% discount on the premium escalation add-on and a one-time onboarding credit. Details in the ratesheet.

I'm looping Marissa for pricing and Karthik for legal/ops constraints on proration and billing language.

Best,

Emily / Procurement team —

Following up with concrete numbers and a short term sheet: see the attached ratesheet. High level pricing for the three SLA bands we discussed (monthly, USD):
- Gold (99.95%): premium escalation add-on $6,000/mo (flat), uptime credits: 10% invoice credit tier at 99.90-99.95%
- Platinum (99.99%): premium escalation add-on $12,000/mo (flat), uptime credits: 20% invoice credit tier under 99.99%
- Enterprise+ (99.995%): bespoke pricing, includes 24x7 named on-call + annual tabletop drills

Proration model we propose (to address your ETL bursts):
- Add-on prorated by days remaining in calendar month when the change is requested via signed amendment
- Credits are applied only to the invoice for the month containing the incident (no cross-month split)
- For customers with predictable burst windows, we can include a rolling buffer of 10% extra capacity for the first 3 months at no additional charge to validate sizing (one-time)

Commercial flexibility to consider: 12-month commit for Gold/Platinum gets you 8–12% on overall platform consumption; 24-month moves to 15%. The premium escalation add-on discount we mentioned earlier applies only to the add-on recurring fee, not to per-incident override time.

Please review and let us know where procurement needs tighter language (proration formula, credits application, measurement window). Happy to hop on a quick call.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa / Aditya —

Thanks for the detail. Procurement has two follow-ups: 1) we need the exact credit formula in contract language (we prefer a deterministic box: credit = (1 - (actual_uptime / SLA_uptime)) * invoice_amount * multiplier); can you confirm Redwood is comfortable committing to a deterministic math expression? 2) We need clarity on how the 10% buffer for bursts is tracked and whether that buffer can be used multiple months in a row without additional charge.

Also, our billing cycles are calendar-month and we insist credits be reflected on the invoice following the incident within the same month (not carried forward). If you charge the add-on prorated mid-month, procurement wants the prorate rounded to the nearest dollar and visible as a separate line item.

If you can provide redline-ready contract language for these two points by COB tomorrow, legal can move quickly.

Best regards,
Acme Analytics Procurement

Subject: Re: SLA tiers + billing/proration question

Thanks — quick answers and next steps: 

1) Deterministic credit formula: Redwood can commit to the following contract language (we will provide as a redline):

   "Credit = MIN(InvoiceAmount, ROUND_TO_CENTS((1 - (ActualMonthlyUptime / SLA_TargetUptime)) * InvoiceAmount * CreditMultiplier))"

   - CreditMultiplier: Gold=1.0, Platinum=1.5 (reflects greater impact for higher tiers). Rationale: gives a predictable ceiling and scales with the invoice.

2) Burst buffer policy: the 10% buffer is a one-time validation allowance for the first 90 days post-deployment. It is not an ongoing free buffer. If Acme wants sustained buffer use beyond 90 days, we can add a predictable overage at a fixed rate (to be included in the SOW). We will document buffer tracking in the monitoring dashboard and include a weekly usage CSV export so procurement can audit.

3) Proration rounding & invoice line: agreed — prorated add-on charges will be rounded to the nearest dollar and appear as an individual line item with the amendment reference. Credits for an incident will be applied to the invoice for the same calendar month and displayed as a credit line item named "SLA Credit - Month YYYY".

Next steps: Marissa will push a redline with the precise language and the numbers you prefer (Gold/Platinum multipliers and any discount tiers). Karthik — can you confirm there are no legal/ops blockers to the multiplier approach? If not, we'll prepare the amendment and a DocuSign link.

If this looks good, I'll schedule a short call with procurement tomorrow at 10am PT to review the redline.

Best,
